Hi Anna —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll pull an annotated control-plane boundary diagram and a one-page isolation summary for Dedicated vs Private. High-level answers to your immediate questions:

- Control-plane telemetry and orchestration signals are carried over our control-plane fabric; for Dedicated deployments customers have the option to run a private control plane that terminates in their VPC (Private control plane) or to use Redwood-managed control plane endpoints that do not see customer model payloads.
- Customer inference payloads (model inputs/outputs) are never stored in the shared control plane; those are routed directly to your Dedicated instance in your isolated tenant pool.
- We will provide a SIG mapping file with the specific SIG/CaiQ question IDs called out for multi-tenancy and boundary controls.

We expect to send a diagram + 1-page summary and the SIG extract by Thu Sep 16. Let me know if the Greenvale auditors need anything stricter (e.g., signed attestation).

Best,
Naomi

Attached are the artifacts you requested for your SOC 2 evidence pack: controlplane-boundary-diagram-v1.png, isolation-model-summary-onepager.pdf, and sig-mapping-extract.xlsx. Short executive summary below you can share with auditors: 

Executive summary (auditor-friendly):
- Deployment modes: Redwood offers two control-plane topologies for Dedicated customers: (1) Redwood-managed control plane (Redwood endpoints in our control plane) and (2) Customer-private control plane (control plane endpoints terminating inside the customer's VPC).
- Data flow guarantees: Customer inference payloads (request/response tokens) are routed directly to the Dedicated tenant pool and are not persisted in the shared control plane. Control-plane telemetry (metrics/health checks) contains operational metadata but does not contain raw model inputs/outputs.
- Network isolation: Dedicated tenant pools are placed in isolated VNets/subnets with restrictive ingress/egress rules. Control-plane management traffic is authenticated and encrypted (mTLS) and uses dedicated service identities. Where customers select a private control plane, control-plane APIs terminate in their VPC via customer-managed endpoints and do not traverse shared backbone segments.
- Multi-tenancy risk controls: Logical tenant separation is enforced at the serving layer with per-tenant authentication tokens and KV cache partitioning. We also provide optional host-level isolation (dedicated node pools) for stricter separation.

Attachments: the diagram includes an annotated legend showing control-plane endpoints, Dedicated tenant pool, customer VPC peering/NAT boundaries, and the data path that excludes raw payload routing through shared telemetry. The SIG mapping spreadsheet calls out the CaiQ/SIG questions we mapped (multi-tenancy, boundary definition, telemetry controls) and references the corresponding Redwood control identifiers.
